activePlan.objective: Two owner-approved follow-ups: extend PR #7's never-merge backstop to PR #9, and make connect-workflow.yml's install/activate flow resumable after a partial failure.
steps: Extend .github/workflows/block-pr-7.yml's block job to fail for PR #7 or #9 (LOCKED_PR_NUMBERS), keeping the file's original name and the 'block' check name so no required-check re-registration is needed.

Update AGENTS.md's absolute branch-policy rule to name PR #9 as current, keeping #7 listed as a harmless historical entry and documenting the replace-by-adding-not-swapping convention for any future successor.
Update test/workflow.test.js's block-pr-7.yml test for the new LOCKED_PR_NUMBERS logic and message text.

Before touching connect-workflow.yml: clarify 'make it never disconnect' with the owner, since the literal request would have meant removing the documented, deliberate design-brief-deletion severing check (an anti-tampering control, not a bug). Confirmed the owner meant install/activate robustness, not removing that check.

Make the install job's governance-file commit step idempotent: an exact-match 'nothing changed' diff (a resumed run after governance files were already committed but Development-branch creation then failed) is treated as done, not as a mismatch to refuse.

Tighten the Development-branch existence check to distinguish git ls-remote --exit-code's exit 2 (branch doesn't exist) from any other nonzero exit (a real failure), rather than treating all nonzero exits as 'safe to create'.
Add a dedicated test for the new resumability behavior; run the full local suite plus every fast/offline audit before pushing.

completed: block-pr-7.yml now fails for PR #7 or PR #9 via LOCKED_PR_NUMBERS='7 9', keeping its filename and 'block' check name unchanged.
AGENTS.md's absolute branch-policy rule now names PR #9, with PR #7 kept as a historical (permanently inert) entry and a documented add-don't-swap convention for future replacements.
connect-workflow.yml's install job no longer refuses a resumed run where the governance files are already correctly in place - only a genuine partial/mismatched diff still fails closed.
connect-workflow.yml's Development-branch existence check now distinguishes 'doesn't exist yet' from 'could not confirm due to a real error', refusing to guess in the latter case.
verification: lint:workflows, docs:check, validate, audit:clutter, audit:privacy, and audit:security all pass.
The activate job's ruleset application was already idempotent (upsert-by-name) and needed no change.
remaining: Push and confirm Self-Test, CodeQL, and AI handoff policy are green.

The owner still needs to add 'block' as a required status check on main (Settings -> Branches -> Branch protection rules) for PR #9's lock to actually GitHub-disable its merge button - no tool available here can do that remotely.

Still blocked on owner-supplied resources, not a code gap: the hosted multi-repository integration workflow and connect-workflow.yml's activate phase both need a real target repository/token to actually be exercised.
Codex's own remaining items still stand: no promotion or branch-protection change is authorized without the owner's explicit instruction beyond what's already been done.
